### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/service-settings`, touching **33** documentable anchor(s).

**7** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/client-sdk.mdx`  _(via getLocales (sdk, the bare tail of client method i18n.getLocales, bound to GET /api/v1/i18n/locales), i18n.getLocales (sdk, the route ledger binds it to GET /api/v1/i18n/locales))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/drivers.mdx`  _(via SettingsService (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/kernel/runtime-services/push-service.mdx`  _(via /devices/:deviceId (route, bridged from symbol getLocales — its route source's handler names it))_
- `content/docs/kernel/services-checklist.mdx`  _(via getLocales (symbol, a method of interface LocaleListService), getLocales (sdk, the bare tail of client method i18n.getLocales, bound to GET /api/v1/i18n/locales), unregisterDevice (sdk, the bare tail of client method notifications.unregisterDevice, bound to DELETE /notifications/devices/:deviceId), /api/v1/i18n/locales (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/config-resolution.mdx`  _(via SettingsService (symbol, a top-level class), registerSettingsRoutes (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/http-protocol.mdx`  _(via getLocales (symbol, a method of interface LocaleListService), getLocales (sdk, the bare tail of client method i18n.getLocales, bound to GET /api/v1/i18n/locales))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/index.mdx`  _(via SettingsService (symbol, a top-level class), SettingsServicePlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via unregisterDevice (sdk, the bare tail of client method notifications.unregisterDevice, bound to DELETE /notifications/devices/:deviceId))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-0.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/i18n/locales (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-3.mdx`  _(via unregisterDevice (sdk, the bare tail of client method notifications.unregisterDevice, bound to DELETE /notifications/devices/:deviceId), /devices/:deviceId (route, bridged from symbol getLocales — its route source's handler names it))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **6** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **219** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **9** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 677ac3bbc026ae9a6d6049b3dd1ad0f5e66bb4d7` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `74481d1eaf566530496115067132dff33de57478` — the merge of head `e1c377ef0e8054f799a13c64482a5b04a998304a` into base `677ac3bbc026ae9a6d6049b3dd1ad0f5e66bb4d7`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 74481d1eaf566530496115067132dff33de57478 && git checkout 74481d1eaf566530496115067132dff33de57478
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 677ac3bbc026ae9a6d6049b3dd1ad0f5e66bb4d7 e1c377ef0e8054f799a13c64482a5b04a998304a && git checkout -B drift-repro 677ac3bbc026ae9a6d6049b3dd1ad0f5e66bb4d7 && git merge --no-ff e1c377ef0e8054f799a13c64482a5b04a998304a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 677ac3bbc026ae9a6d6049b3dd1ad0f5e66bb4d7
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 677ac3bbc026ae9a6d6049b3dd1ad0f5e66bb4d7` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `e1c377ef0e8054f799a13c64482a5b04a998304a`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/services/service-settings/src/index.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/localization-locale-options.test.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/localization-locale-options.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/manifests/localization.manifest.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-routes.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-service-plugin.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-service.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-service.types.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/translations/zh-CN.ts + packages/spec/src/system/platform-locales.ts, packages/spec/src/system/settings-manifest.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/system/settings-manifest.test.ts, packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.ts, packages/core/src/fallbacks/memory-i18n.ts, packages/services/service-i18n/src/file-i18n-adapter.ts, packages/runtime/src/app-plugin.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/i18n.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/translations/settings-translation-coverage.test.ts, packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/phone-sms-texts.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/idp-locale-claim.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/email-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-writers.ts, packages/runtime/src/seed-locale.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/current-user-endpoints.ts, ui/apps/console/src/pages/settings/SettingsField.tsx, ui/apps/console/src/pages/settings/useSettingsLabel.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/layout/LocaleSwitcher.tsx, ui/packages/i18n/src/provider.tsx

Inputs: card #30286 (body, 5 comments through the dev report 6657161883), PR #30446 (body, 10-file list, net diff against `main` at the merge base `dbf53efe`), the check-runs on the head (read at 2026-11-05T12:07Z; the last five `Test Core` shards were still running at the first read and were re-read before this verdict). The cited code was read with `git show` on the head's objects — no checkout, build, test or gate run.

### ① Derived judgments

Each accept-set or public-surface change the diff implies, named right or wrong against the code read:

1. **Save of `localization.locale` (`validatePatch` → `optionTableOf`)**: accepted set = the i18n service's `getLocales()` codes, plus a stored spelling that `platformLocaleTagOf` maps to the same platform-table language as an offered code (`en-US` where `en`, `zh-CN` where `zh-Hans`/`zh`, `ja-JP` where `ja`, `es-ES` where `es`). The declared four stand only when the source answers nothing (no `i18n` service, empty list, or a throw). **Right.** The offered set is read at each call, never cached, so a translation item added at runtime on a non-declaring deployment is accepted at once; on a deployment that declares `i18n.supportedLocales` the list IS the declaration (`file-i18n-adapter.ts:244`, `memory-i18n.ts:220`), and the console's language menu reads the same list through `GET /api/v1/i18n/locales` (`provider.tsx:784`, filtered only by `canResolveLanguage`, which admits any well-formed tag once a loader is wired). Same source, same freezing behaviour on both ends.
2. **`OS_LOCALIZATION_LOCALE` (`effectiveEnvOverride` → `optionTableOf`)**: judged against the same table on every read; the registration-time audit skips a sourced key. **Right in steady state**; see ④-S2 for the boot window.
3. **Stored value outside the set**: no read, boot, env or unrelated-patch path re-judges it. `validatePatch`'s TOUCH gate is unchanged (options check sits inside it; no `localization` specifier declares a `visible` that names `locale`), `get`/`getMany` never consult the table, `auditEnvOverrides` judges env only, and no write path rewrites a row. The namespace read serves it as an extra option labelled `NAME (no longer offered)` in the reader's language, and a re-write of it is refused. **Right.**
4. **Legacy spellings**: `en-US` (the manifest default) is admitted on every deployment whose list says `en`, through `PLATFORM_LOCALE_READ_ALIASES`; without this the default itself would be outside the set on all three `examples/*`. **Right.** A code the table does not name is exact-match only (`fr-FR` is not `fr`) — see ④-S3.
5. **Public surface**: `SettingsService.registerOptionSource(namespace, key, source)` (new, last-registration-wins like `registerAction`), `getNamespace(ns, ctx, display?)` (third optional argument, source-compatible), and `index.ts` exports `SettingsOptionSource`, `SettingsOptionSourceAnswer`, `SettingsServedOption` as types. Additive; no published export removed or retyped; `service-settings` has no `api-surface/` snapshot to regenerate. **Right.** The PR body and changeset name all of them.
6. **`GET /api/settings/:namespace`** serves a copy of the manifest with the sourced key's options replaced; the registered manifest object is untouched (`servedManifest`). **Right.** `GET /api/settings` (`listManifests`) and `getManifest()` still state the declared four — see ④-S1.
7. **Failure mode**: a throwing source is answered as absent, logged once per `namespace.key:cause` at `warn`; an absent `i18n` service (`ctx.getService` throwing or returning `undefined`) is answered as absent. Fail-open to the declared four, never fail-closed, never a crash. **Right**, and the safer direction for a save door.
8. **Translations**: the four `zh-CN` option labels removed so the served self-names show (`useSettingsLabel.ts:154` prefers the bundle key over the served label; the coverage test excludes option labels by its own header, lines 17–20; `en`, `ja-JP`, `es-ES` carried none). **Right.**
9. **Readers of the setting** (the card's question): `resolve-authz-context.ts` (`coerceLocale` is trim-only; `Intl` takes any tag), `auth-plugin.ts` / `auth-manager.ts` (`normalizeAuthEmailLocale` passes a regional tag through unchanged; `EmailService` falls to `DEFAULT_TEMPLATE_LOCALE` `en-US`), `phone-sms-texts.ts` (`phoneSmsLocaleChain` ends at `en`), `seed-locale.ts` (unmatched locale ⇒ unscoped datasets), `audit-writers.ts` (`t()` falls back), `current-user-endpoints.ts` (echo). None refuses, throws or misformats on a locale outside the four. **The dev's table is accurate.** One comment in `auth-manager.ts:1270` states an invariant this diff retires — ④-S4.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/30286-default-language-follows-deployment.md`: `@objectstack/service-settings: patch`, `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, `**BREAKING**` banner with Before / Now / Unchanged / Remedy, one ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. The PR body carries the same two declaration lines; the title carries `!`. Per AGENTS.md step 3 a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch` with its banner and disposition, and `none` takes `patch`; the additive exports do not move the kind. `Check Changeset`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates` and `Lint · PM dispatch-gates` are green on the head. **Matches what the diff publishes.** `Clause-②:` the `(narrowing)` arm is the right one: `ja-JP` / `es-ES` on `examples/app-showcase` and `examples/app-crm` (`supportedLocales: ['en', 'zh-CN']`) were accepted and are refused; the Claim's `yes (widening)` was superseded with the seat's agreement, as the dev report says.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions: []` — nothing to answer.
- Dev deviation 1, narrowing instead of widening: judged in ② and ④; agreed with the seat before code.
- Dev deviation 2, shared files: `settings-service.ts` hunks are at `auditEnvOverrides`, `effectiveEnvOverride`, the new block after `registerLiveStatus`, `getNamespace` and `validatePatch`; the `setMany` write loop (the `effectiveEnvOverride` env-lock throw at 2516) is **not** touched. Seat 2's #30448 (card #30385) also edits `settings-service.ts` and `settings-service.types.ts`; no hunk overlaps, but both add to the same files, so whichever lands second rebases. Not a finding against this PR.
- Dev deviation 3, pins in the component's own test file rather than `settings-routes.test.ts`: consistent with ruling 6583487846 (a new behaviour's pins in their own `describe`, no new shared harness).
- `ui/**` half: none remains. `SettingsField.tsx:630` draws `spec.options` from the namespace read and `renderOptionLabel` falls back to the served label. Verified, not taken from the PR body.
- The card's `#30206` note: the first-run checklist is open and not in the tree; the list it should read is the namespace read's served `locale` options (see ④-S1 for why not `GET /api/settings`).
- Fork check: head repo is `objectstack-ai/objectstack`. Governed surfaces: none in the file list. `Governed Surface Queue Guard` green.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing, read against the published spec on `main`. `settings-manifest.zod.ts:496` says that without `valueDomain` the `options` table is exhaustive and "legal means this deployment ships an adapter for it"; `settings-manifest.test.ts:210` refused `bcp47_locale` precisely because `localization.locale`'s options "ARE the shipped message catalogs — a registry-backed table". The manifest's literal four were a stand-in for that registry. This diff makes the spec's own refusal real at the consumer: the accepted set becomes the deployment's locale list. The capability taken away (`ja-JP` as the default on a deployment that declares only `en`/`zh-CN`) was already dead one step downstream — that deployment's users could not pick Japanese in the menu, and `GET /auth/me/localization` would hand every renderer a language it cannot show. Not a capability declared and withheld; a declaration made true. The maintainer's word on the card (「立卡」 over the Expected list, "the server accepts exactly those values") rules it. **The narrowing holds.**

Tried to break it:

- Stale stored value on a save of another key — TOUCH gate, held. On boot — no stored-row validation anywhere, held. On env override — env value judged, stored row untouched, held. Served to the page with the stored spelling kept — held (`options[sameLanguage]` keeps the stored value so the select shows it chosen).
- Source throws mid-save — declared table, one `warn`, held. `i18n` missing — `ctx.getService` guarded both ways, held.
- Source registered after a manifest — the audit would have judged the declared table; JSDoc says register first and the plugin does. Held for the one registration there is.
- `Intl.DisplayNames` absent, malformed tag, unnamed tag — code returned, held; capitalisation matches `LocaleSwitcher.localeLabel`.

Findings, none a must-fix:

- **S1 (should-fix, follow-up card)** — Two statements of the table remain: `getManifest()`, `listManifests()` and `GET /api/settings` still carry the declared four as `options`, while only the namespace read serves the live list. The spec doc at `settings-manifest.zod.ts:490–500` still describes the declared `options` as the save boundary for every select without a domain. A consumer reading the manifest list (the Setup hub, `#30206`'s language row, an SDK caller) is told a table that is not the one the save judges. `packages/spec/**` is outside this dispatch; the seat should file the spec card that either notes the option-source carve-out beside `valueDomain` or lets `listManifests` serve sourced options too.
- **S2 (should-fix)** — Boot window on the env door. `app-plugin.ts` applies `setSupportedLocales` and the app bundles in `start()`, and every platform plugin (this one included, `settings-service-plugin.ts:299–315`) pushes its bundle at `kernel:ready`. On a deployment that declares nothing, a `kernel:ready` reader (`auth-plugin.ts:1333` `applyLocalizationLocale`, `seed-locale.ts:137`) can ask before the list is whole, get the declared four, see `OS_LOCALIZATION_LOCALE=vi-VN` IGNORED and record that locale (`setDefaultSmsLocale`, `applyEmailLocale`) until the next settings-change event — an env override coming into force a tick later fires none. `reportRejectedEnvOverride` also dedupes on `env=value`, so its one error line says IGNORED for the boot's lifetime while later reads put the override in force. AGENTS.md "Startup registry reads" class. Narrow (env override + locale outside the four + non-declaring deployment), and pre-PR the same value was always refused, so no regression — but the new capability is only delivered after the boot settles. A ready-time re-read or a source that answers `undefined` until `kernel:ready` would close it.
- **S3 (should-fix)** — Two matchers in one product. `admits` is exact match plus `platformLocaleTagOf`; `idp-locale-claim.ts` closes a locale against the same `getLocales()` with `resolveLocale` (exact → case → base → variant), and `runtime/src/domains/i18n.ts` falls back on translations the same way. So `sys_user.locale` can hold `fr` (resolved from `fr-FR`) while Setup refuses `fr-FR` where `fr` is offered, and `admits` is case-sensitive where `resolveLocale` is not. No stored legacy value is affected (the four are all table-aliased), so this is a consistency point, not a narrowing fault; naming the chosen matcher once, or reusing `resolveLocale`, is the fix.
- **S4 (should-fix)** — `auth-manager.ts:1266–1272`: "`AUTH_EMAIL_TEMPLATE_LOCALES` … are also the four options the `localization.locale` setting offers, so the two ends agree by construction". After this diff they agree by `normalizeAuthEmailLocale`'s pass-through and `EmailService`'s `en-US` rung, not by construction. The reader still behaves (judged in ①-9); the comment now states a retired invariant. Outside the dispatch's file surface; one-line follow-up.

Check-runs on the head at the final read: every completed run is `success` or `skipped`, `Test Core` shards included; none `failure`, `cancelled` or `timed_out`.

**VERDICT: PASS**

## 维护者速读

1. 改了什么：Setup → 本地化 →「默认语言」不再写死四种，改成部署实际支持的语言，和语言菜单读同一来源（i18n `getLocales()`），每次打开和保存时现读，后加的翻译项马上可选；选项用该语言自己的名字显示。
2. 为什么改：法语包完整、用户菜单能选法语，但组织默认语言只能在英/中/日/西里选，存 `fr-FR`、`vi-VN` 被拒，新用户都从公司没选的语言起步。
3. 风险：收窄，部署不支持的语言以后存不进去（如应用只声明 `en`、`zh-CN` 时的 `ja-JP`）；已存旧值照常生效可读、标「（已不再提供）」，保存别的字段不受影响；`en-US` 等老写法在提供 `en` 时照常接受；没有 i18n 服务时仍用原来四种。
4. 先看：`service-settings/src/localization-locale-options.ts`，以及 `settings-service.ts` 新的 `registerOptionSource` / `optionTableOf` / `servedManifest`。
5. 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-settings exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/localization-locale-options.test.ts`，14 条全绿。
6. 需要你做的：无，席位落地。合约审查 PASS 6657571849 在案，四条 should-fix 已立卡 #30455、#30456；按 maintainer 13:47Z「技能不需要我审核的不应该等我」，不属 Tier H、不超 3000 行。
